I've been farming this 10.1 mu for twenty years now, so I mostly do what worked last year. My son is in the city, so it's just me and my wife working the land. I'm getting old, 72 now, but wheat-maize is what everyone does here in Quzhou, and I know the rhythm.

For wheat, I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use the improved seed they sell at the供销社 — Jimai or Shimai variety, whatever the shop has, about 15 kg per mu because I broadcast a bit thick in case of winter kill. I plough the land after maize harvest, not that no-till stuff the young ones talk about. Before sowing I spread 2 bags of 复合肥 (compound 15-15-15), that's 100 kg per mu — my neighbor Old Wang does the same. Then in spring when it greens up, I put down 1 bag of 尿素, 40 kg per mu. I'd rather put a little extra than see my wheat turn yellow. I water 3 times from the well: once after planting, once at jointing in spring, once at filling. One spray for aphids and powdery mildew usually, sometimes two if it's humid. I expect about 450-500 kg per mu if the weather is fair.

For maize in summer, I plant right after wheat harvest, no time to waste. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type, about 2.5 kg per mu. I use rotary tiller and sow directly. I put 1 bag of compound fertilizer at planting, 50 kg per mu, then at big trumpet stage I side-dress urea, another 30 kg per mu. Summer maize needs less water than wheat because of the rains, but I still irrigate 2 times from the well when it's dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer. I get around 500-550 kg per mu usually.

I don't waste money but I don't cut corners on fertilizer. A bad harvest is a disaster — wasting 10 yuan of urea is nothing compared to losing 100 kg of grain.
